# USB Full-Speed Device Interface Module Specification

## 1. Overview

The module implements a USB 2.0 Full-Speed (12 Mbps) device interface. It acts as a memory-mapped peripheral on a system bus and provides a complete USB device-side interface, including endpoint control, packet buffering, interrupt generation, link-state detection, and physical-layer I/O control.

The module is intended to be used with an external USB transceiver or with directly connected USB pads. It supports:

- Full-Speed USB 2.0 device operation at 12 Mbps.
- A 2 kB packet buffer, organized as 32 buffers of 64 bytes each.
- Up to 12 endpoints, including endpoint 0.
- SETUP, IN, and OUT transactions.
- Bulk, control, interrupt, and isochronous transfers.
- Software-configurable D+/D- pin flipping.
- Multiple transmit and receive PHY interface modes.

The module spans multiple clock and power domains. Behavior that crosses these domains is synchronized internally, and software-visible effects may take a few clock cycles to propagate.

## 2. Clocks and Resets

The module operates from three clock domains:

- A system/bus clock for register access, interrupts, and one port of the packet buffer.
- A 48 MHz USB clock for USB packet reception, transmission, and link-state detection.
- An always-on clock for wake event and power-management signaling.

The module shall have reset inputs for each clock domain. Each reset shall initialize all state in that domain to a safe default. After reset:

- The device shall be disabled.
- No pullup shall be asserted on D+ or D-.
- The USB device address shall be zero.
- Interrupts shall be cleared.
- Software-visible status registers shall return their reset values.
- Outputs to the USB pins shall be in a benign, high-impedance or disabled state.

Once the system reset is released, the module shall assert an output indicating that the module has come out of reset. This indication shall remain asserted until the next reset.

## 3. Software Configuration and Register Interface

Software configures the module through a memory-mapped register interface. The register interface shall provide access to:

- Device-level control, such as enabling the device and setting the USB device address.
- Per-endpoint configuration, including IN/OUT enable, stall, isochronous mode, buffer selection, and data-toggle clear.
- Endpoint reception enables for OUT and SETUP packets.
- FIFO status and data registers for packet buffer management.
- Interrupt enable, status, and test registers.
- PHY configuration, including pin flip, receiver selection, transmit encoding, oscillator test mode, and SOF reference disable.
- Wake configuration and wake event status.

The module shall also expose a memory window to the internal packet buffer. Software shall be able to read and write packet data through this window using the bus protocol.

Software writes to the available-buffer FIFO shall be accepted until the FIFO is full. If software attempts to write a buffer ID when the FIFO is full, the write shall be ignored and an overflow event shall be reported.

A read from the received-buffer FIFO shall return the oldest received-packet record and pop that record from the FIFO. If the FIFO is empty, the read shall return zero-filled data. The FIFO shall provide status information indicating whether it is empty, full, or partially filled.

## 4. USB Device Enable and Attachment

The device shall remain detached from the USB bus until software enables it. When enabled, the module shall assert the appropriate Full-Speed pullup:

- If pin flip is disabled, the pullup shall be presented on D+.
- If pin flip is enabled, the pullup shall be presented on D-.

Only one pullup shall be asserted at any time. The pullup shall be removed when the device is disabled.

The module shall monitor the VBUS sense input. When VBUS is present and the device is enabled, the module shall consider the link powered. When VBUS is not present, or when the device is disabled, the module shall consider the link disconnected and report this state to software.

## 5. USB Link-State Detection and Events

The module shall detect and report the following USB link states:

- Disconnected.
- Powered.
- Powered Suspended.
- Active No SOF.
- Active.
- Suspended.
- Resuming.

The current link state shall be visible to software.

The module shall generate events and raise interrupts for these link-state changes:

- Device powered.
- Device disconnected.
- USB bus reset detected.
- USB suspend detected.
- USB resume detected.
- Host lost.

A bus reset shall be detected when the D+ and D- lines are both low for at least 3 µs. On a bus reset, the module shall:

- Report the reset event to software.
- Clear the configured USB device address back to zero.
- Cancel all pending IN transactions by clearing their ready bit.
- Mark any canceled IN transactions as pending so software can requeue them later.

A suspend shall be detected when the bus is idle in the J state for more than 3 ms. When suspended, the module shall:

- Report the suspend event to software.
- Assert a transceiver suspend indication.
- Automatically disable the differential receiver output enable.

A resume event shall be reported when the link leaves the suspended state. If software requests a resume, the module shall transmit the required resume signaling.

Host-lost shall be reported when the link is active but no Start-of-Frame (SOF) packet is received for four consecutive 1.005 ms frame-detection windows. The host is required to send SOF packets every 1 ms, so this condition indicates that the host is no longer communicating.

## 6. Packet Reception (OUT and SETUP Transactions)

The module shall receive OUT and SETUP packets on endpoints for which software has enabled reception. Software may also configure an endpoint to accept both OUT and SETUP traffic, or only one type.

When a valid OUT or SETUP packet is received on an enabled endpoint, the module shall:

1. Take the next buffer ID from the available-buffer FIFO.
2. Store the received data bytes into the packet buffer at that buffer ID.
3. Store the packet byte count, endpoint number, and a setup/out indication into the received-buffer FIFO.
4. Return an ACK handshake to the host.
5. Raise a packet-received interrupt.

The reported packet size shall not include the CRC bytes. If the CRC bytes fit within the buffer, they may be stored after the data bytes.

If no buffer is available, or if the received-buffer FIFO is full, the module shall not accept the packet. Instead, it shall return a NAK to the host so the host retries later.

If the endpoint is not enabled for reception, or is stalled, the module shall not accept the packet. It shall return either a NAK or a STALL handshake as appropriate.

If a received packet has a bad CRC, a bad PID, or a bit-stuff error, the module shall:

- Not ACK the packet.
- Not write the packet data into the received-buffer FIFO.
- Raise the corresponding receive-error interrupt.

The available-buffer FIFO depth and received-buffer FIFO depth shall be visible to software, along with full and empty status. The module shall raise an interrupt when the received-buffer FIFO is non-empty. It shall also raise an interrupt if the available-buffer FIFO becomes empty or if software writes to it when it is full.

## 7. Packet Transmission (IN Transactions)

Software shall be able to queue a packet for transmission on a configured IN endpoint by:

1. Writing the data into a free packet buffer.
2. Writing the buffer ID, byte count, and a ready bit for that endpoint.

When the host sends an IN token to that endpoint, the module shall transmit the packet data from the buffer, followed by the generated CRC. If the host ACKs the packet:

- The ready bit for that endpoint shall be cleared.
- A sent indication shall be set for that endpoint.
- A packet-sent interrupt shall be raised.

If the host does not ACK the packet, the module shall retry the transmission on the next IN token to that endpoint.

If no data is queued for an IN endpoint, the module shall return a NAK. If the endpoint is stalled, it shall return a STALL.

When a SETUP packet is received on an endpoint that has a pending IN transmission, the module shall cancel that transmission: it shall clear the ready bit and set the pending bit for that endpoint. This allows software to requeue the transmission after the control transfer completes. A bus reset shall cancel pending IN transmissions on all endpoints in the same way.

## 8. Endpoint Stalls

Software may configure each endpoint to stall IN and/or OUT transactions. When an endpoint is stalled:

- IN requests to that endpoint shall receive a STALL handshake.
- OUT requests to that endpoint shall receive a STALL handshake.

The stall behavior shall remain in effect until the next SETUP packet is received on that endpoint, or until software clears the stall configuration. When a SETUP packet is received on a stalled endpoint, the module shall automatically clear the stall configuration for that endpoint. This allows the device to respond to the SETUP and lets software decide how to handle the new control transfer.

## 9. Control Transfer Behavior

The module shall support control transfers by treating SETUP packets as a special form of received packet. A SETUP packet shall be reported to software through the received-buffer FIFO with an indication that it is a SETUP packet.

When a SETUP packet is received on an endpoint:

- Any pending IN transmission on that endpoint shall be canceled (ready cleared, pending set).
- Any stall configuration for that endpoint shall be cleared.

After a SETUP packet is received and before software configures a response, the module shall return NAK to IN/OUT requests on that endpoint. Software then configures the endpoint for the data and status stages of the control transfer.

## 10. Data Toggle Handling

The module shall maintain data-toggle state for each endpoint as required by the USB 2.0 protocol. It shall correctly toggle the data PID on successful IN and OUT transfers.

Software shall be able to clear the data-toggle state for selected endpoints. This is useful after a bus reset or for protocol management. The clearing operation shall take effect in the USB clock domain within a bounded synchronization delay after software writes the control registers.

## 11. Packet Buffer Behavior

The packet buffer shall be a single 2 kB memory that is accessible from both the system bus and the USB interface. It shall be organized as 32 buffers of 64 bytes each.

Software shall be able to read and write any byte in the packet buffer through the memory-mapped window. The USB engine shall be able to read packet data for IN transmissions and write received packet data for OUT and SETUP transactions. The two access ports shall be independent, allowing the system bus and the USB engine to access the buffer concurrently.

If software and the USB engine access the same buffer simultaneously, there shall be no corruption of data beyond normal dual-port RAM arbitration behavior. Software is responsible for coordinating buffer ownership using the available-buffer and received-buffer FIFOs.

## 12. Interrupts

The module shall generate interrupt outputs for the following events:

- Packet received.
- Packet sent.
- Device powered.
- Device disconnected.
- Host lost.
- Link reset.
- Link suspend.
- Link resume.
- Available-buffer FIFO empty.
- Received-buffer FIFO full.
- Available-buffer FIFO overflow.
- Link IN error.
- Link OUT error.
- Receive CRC error.
- Receive PID error.
- Receive bit-stuff error.
- SOF frame received.

Each interrupt shall be independently maskable. The module shall provide interrupt enable, interrupt status, and interrupt test registers. Software can read the interrupt status to determine which event occurred, write to clear the status, and write a test bit to generate a software-induced interrupt.

Events that cross from the USB clock domain to the system clock domain shall be presented as single pulses so that one event produces one interrupt request.

## 13. SOF Reference Outputs

The module shall provide two reference outputs relating to SOF packet reception:

- A reference pulse output that pulses once for each successfully received SOF packet.
- A reference valid output that indicates whether the reference pulse output can be trusted.

Both outputs shall be synchronous to the 48 MHz USB clock.

The reference pulse shall be generated on every SOF packet unless SOF reference generation is disabled by software. The first reference pulse after the link becomes active also asserts the reference valid output. The reference valid output shall remain asserted as long as SOF packets continue to be received and the link remains active. In a cycle without a reference pulse, it shall be deasserted when:

- The link is no longer active.
- The host is lost.
- SOF reference generation is disabled by software.

The reference valid output shall be reasserted after the next valid SOF packet.

These outputs are intended to allow an external clock-calibration unit to synchronize the 48 MHz clock source.

## 14. Physical Interface Behavior

The module shall provide outputs for driving the D+ and D- USB lines. During transmission, the D+ and D- output drivers shall be enabled. When not transmitting, the outputs shall be disabled or high-impedance so that an external transceiver or pads can drive the bus.

The module shall support two transmit encodings:

1. A direct encoding in which D+ and D- are driven with the USB differential values.
2. An alternate encoding in which the module drives a data signal and a separate SE0 signal.

Software shall select the transmit encoding. The module shall also provide an output that indicates which transmit interface is currently selected.

For reception, the module shall support two input modes:

1. A differential receiver mode, in which the recovered serial data is taken from a differential receiver output.
2. A direct mode, in which the J and K states are recovered from the D+ and D- inputs directly.

The D+ and D- inputs shall always be used to detect the SE0 state, regardless of the selected receive mode.

The module shall provide a differential receiver enable output. This output shall be asserted when differential receive mode is selected by software. It shall be automatically deasserted while the device is suspended.

The module shall provide transceiver control outputs:

- A suspend indication that is asserted when the device is in the USB suspend state.
- Pullup control outputs for D+ and D- as described earlier.

The module shall support software-controlled D+/D- pin flipping. When pin flip is enabled, the internal D+ and D- paths shall be swapped and the pullup shall be presented on the external D- line.

## 15. Wake and Always-On Behavior

The module shall interface with the always-on power domain to support USB wake detection and system wake signaling.

It shall provide:

- A wake enable output, controlled by software.
- A wake acknowledge output, which pulses when software acknowledges a wake event.

The module shall capture asynchronous events from the always-on domain and make them visible to software. These events include:

- A detected USB bus reset.
- Loss of VBUS sense.
- Debug state information from the wake detection logic.

The captured status shall be updated even when the system clock domain has been reset or is not running, as appropriate for the always-on functionality.

## 16. Alerts

The module shall provide alert outputs for reporting integrity failures. In particular, an alert shall be asserted if a bus integrity error is detected on the register interface.

The module shall support alert testing through software. When the alert test bit is set, the module shall exercise the alert path in the same way as a real alert event.

If multiple alert outputs are instantiated, each shall follow the same alert source and shall be independently testable and configurable for asynchronous operation.

## 17. Summary of Key Behavioral Requirements

- The module shall operate as a USB 2.0 Full-Speed device interface.
- It shall not operate in High-Speed or Low-Speed modes.
- It shall support up to 12 endpoints and packets up to 64 bytes.
- It shall provide a 2 kB packet buffer with software access via the bus and USB access via the USB clock domain.
- It shall generate all listed interrupts and status indications.
- It shall correctly detect and report USB link states and events.
- It shall support software control of endpoint enable, stall, data toggle, buffer management, and PHY configuration.
- It shall provide synchronized behavior for signals crossing clock domains, and it shall ensure that one event produces one interrupt.
- It shall provide SOF reference outputs for clock calibration.
- It shall provide wake and always-on signaling for system power management.

# Behavioral Specification: USB Link State Detector

## 1. Overview

This module tracks the state of a Full-Speed USB link and reports link events to the rest of the design. It observes:

- USB VBUS presence
- Whether the device pull-up is enabled
- The D+/D- line state, including idle (J), non-idle, and single-ended zero (SE0)
- Valid Start-of-Frame (SOF) packets
- Software resume requests

From these observations, the module produces:

- The current USB link state
- Level indications for disconnected, powered, active, suspended, reset, and host-lost conditions
- Pulse indications for resume and missed SOF events

All behavior is synchronous to the 48 MHz USB clock. Long timing intervals are measured using the microsecond tick input.

## 2. USB Link States

The module reports the link state using a 3-bit encoded value. The valid state encodings are:

| Code | Link State | Description |
|------|------------|-------------|
| 000 | Disconnected | VBUS is not present, or the pull-up is disabled. The device is effectively unplugged. |
| 001 | Powered | VBUS is present and the pull-up is enabled, but the device has not yet been reset by the host. |
| 010 | Powered Suspended | The link is suspended before the device has been reset. |
| 011 | Active | The link has been reset and is operating normally; SOF packets are being received. |
| 100 | Suspended | The link was active and has now been suspended due to idle signaling. |
| 101 | Active No SOF | The link has been reset and is active, but no valid SOF packet has been observed yet. |
| 110 | Resuming | Resume signaling is in progress, and the module is waiting for the end of resume signaling. |

The value `111` is reserved and shall not be output.

## 3. Outputs

The module provides the following observable outputs:

| Output | Type | Behavior |
|--------|------|----------|
| Disconnected | Level | Asserted when the current link state is `Disconnected`. |
| Power Present | Level | Asserted when the filtered VBUS sense indicates that VBUS is present. This is independent of the pull-up enable and of the current link state. |
| Reset | Level | Asserted when a valid USB reset is being observed. |
| Active | Level | Asserted when the link state is `Active` or `Active No SOF`. |
| Suspend | Level | Asserted when the link state is `Powered Suspended` or `Suspended`. |
| Resume | Pulse | Asserted for one 48 MHz clock cycle when a resume event completes or when the link leaves a pre-reset suspended state due to bus activity. |
| Missed SOF | Pulse | Asserted for one 48 MHz clock cycle each time the SOF timeout expires while the link is active and no reset is present. |
| Host Lost | Level | Asserted after four consecutive missed-SOF pulses while the link remains active. Cleared when a valid SOF is received, when the link leaves the active state, or on reset. |

## 4. Link State Behavior

The state machine behavior is described by the following transitions.

### 4.1 Disconnected

- If filtered VBUS sense is absent, or the pull-up enable is deasserted, the link shall remain in `Disconnected`.
- When filtered VBUS sense is present and the pull-up enable is asserted, the link shall enter `Powered`.

### 4.2 Any State With Power Loss or Pull-Up Disable

If the filtered VBUS sense goes low, or if the pull-up enable is deasserted, the link shall immediately enter `Disconnected` regardless of the current state. This condition takes priority over all other state transitions.

### 4.3 Powered

While in `Powered`:

- If a valid USB reset completes, the link shall enter `Active No SOF`.
- If a software resume request pulse is received, the link shall enter `Resuming`.
- If the bus remains idle for 3 ms, the link shall enter `Powered Suspended`.

### 4.4 Powered Suspended

While in `Powered Suspended`:

- If a valid USB reset completes, the link shall enter `Active No SOF`.
- If the bus leaves the idle state, the module shall assert the resume pulse and enter `Powered`.

### 4.5 Active No SOF

While in `Active No SOF`:

- If a valid SOF packet is received, the link shall enter `Active`.
- If the bus remains idle for 3 ms, the link shall enter `Suspended`.
- If a USB reset is observed, no state transition is needed because the link is already in the post-reset active state.

### 4.6 Active

While in `Active`:

- If a valid USB reset completes, the link shall enter `Active No SOF`.
- If the bus remains idle for 3 ms, the link shall enter `Suspended`.
- Receiving a valid SOF keeps the link in `Active` and clears missed-SOF tracking.

### 4.7 Suspended

While in `Suspended`:

- If the bus leaves the idle state, the link shall enter `Resuming`.
- If a valid USB reset completes, the module shall assert the resume pulse and enter `Active No SOF`.

### 4.8 Resuming

While in `Resuming`:

- If a J state is detected, indicating the end of resume signaling, the module shall assert the resume pulse and enter `Active No SOF`.
- If a valid USB reset completes, the module shall assert the resume pulse and enter `Active No SOF`.

## 5. Bus State Detection

### 5.1 SE0 Detection

The module shall recognize SE0 only when both D+ and D- are low and the local transmitter is not driving the bus. This prevents the device’s own transmissions from being interpreted as a bus reset.

Raw SE0 indications shall be debounced before being used. A short SE0 pulse that does not persist for the debounce interval shall not trigger reset detection.

### 5.2 VBUS Sense Filtering

The raw VBUS sense shall be debounced before it is used to determine power presence or disconnection. A power loss is acted upon only after the filtered sense indicates that VBUS is no longer present.

### 5.3 Bus Idle and Bus Activity

The module uses a continuous-J detection input to determine whether the bus is idle.

- When the continuous-J indication is asserted, the bus is considered idle.
- When the continuous-J indication is not asserted, the bus is considered active/non-idle.

A J detection input is used to recognize the end of resume signaling.

## 6. Reset Detection

A valid USB reset is defined as an SE0 condition that remains continuously present for at least 3 µs.

- If SE0 ends before 3 µs, no reset shall be reported.
- Once the 3 µs threshold is reached, the reset output shall be asserted and shall remain asserted while the SE0 condition continues.
- When the SE0 condition is released after a valid reset, a reset event shall be generated. This event causes the state transitions described above.
- The reset output shall deassert after the SE0 release is processed.

## 7. Suspend Detection

The module shall monitor for suspend only when VBUS is present and the current link state is one of:

- `Powered`
- `Active No SOF`
- `Active`

If the bus remains continuously idle for 3 ms while in one of these states, the module shall generate a suspend event and enter the corresponding suspended state.

Any bus activity before the 3 ms interval expires shall cancel and restart the idle timing.

## 8. Resume Behavior

Resume is detected when the bus leaves the idle state after being suspended.

- From `Powered Suspended`, bus activity causes an immediate resume pulse and a transition to `Powered`.
- From `Suspended`, bus activity causes a transition to `Resuming`. The resume pulse is generated when the end of resume signaling is observed.
- From `Powered`, a software resume request pulse causes a transition to `Resuming`. The resume pulse is generated when the end of resume signaling is observed.
- From `Suspended`, a reset also causes a resume pulse and a transition to `Active No SOF`.

## 9. SOF and Host Loss Monitoring

While the link is active and no reset is present, the module shall monitor for valid SOF packets.

- If no valid SOF is observed for 1005 µs, the module shall assert a missed-SOF pulse.
- The missed-SOF timer shall restart after each missed-SOF pulse, so the pulse may repeat every 1005 µs while the condition persists.
- Receiving a valid SOF shall clear the missed-SOF timer and the missed-SOF count.
- If four consecutive missed-SOF pulses occur without an intervening valid SOF, the module shall assert the host-lost level.
- Once host-lost is asserted, subsequent missed-SOF pulses shall not change the host-lost state.
- Host-lost shall be cleared when:
  - a valid SOF is received,
  - the link leaves the active state,
  - or a reset is observed.
- Missed-SOF monitoring shall be disabled when the link is not active or when a reset is present.

## 10. Reset Behavior

On reset:

- The link state shall be `Disconnected`.
- The reset, active, suspend, resume, missed-SOF, and host-lost outputs shall be deasserted.
- The disconnected output shall be asserted because the link state is `Disconnected`.
- All internal timing and missed-SOF tracking shall be cleared.

# USB Full-Speed Device Interface Module Specification

## 1. Scope

This specification describes the behavior of the USB-side interface core used by the Full-Speed USB device. The module is clocked from the 48 MHz USB clock and implements the low-level USB packet interface, packet-buffer data movement, endpoint handshaking, frame timing, and USB link-state reporting.

The module supports a configurable number of endpoints, a configurable packet-buffer size, and a maximum USB packet size of 64 bytes. The behavior described here applies to all supported configurations.

## 2. General Behavior

The module shall:

- Operate as a USB 2.0 Full-Speed device interface at 12 Mbps.
- Perform all timing and protocol functions synchronously to the 48 MHz clock.
- Provide the USB-side data path between the USB transceiver and the packet SRAM.
- Manage the flow of received packet information into the receive FIFO.
- Manage the flow of transmit packet data from the packet SRAM in response to IN transactions.
- Maintain and report USB link state, frame number, and protocol error conditions.

## 3. USB Transceiver Interface

The module shall provide a transmit interface suitable for driving an external USB transceiver. This interface includes:

- A data output encoding the K/J state of the bus.
- A single-ended zero output used to indicate the SE0 state.
- An output-enable indication that is active only while the module is driving the USB bus.

During normal packet transmission, the module shall generate the USB serial bitstream with the required Full-Speed signaling, including bit-stuffing and NRZI encoding. While the module is not transmitting, it shall not drive the bus.

The module shall support multiple receive configurations:

- It shall accept single-ended D+ and D− inputs.
- It shall accept an optional differential receiver data input.
- When configured to use the differential receiver, the module shall recover K/J data from the differential receiver input.
- When not configured to use the differential receiver, the module shall recover K/J data from the single-ended D+/D− inputs.
- The D+/D− inputs shall always be used to detect the SE0 state.

The end-of-packet detection behavior shall be configurable:

- In normal mode, EOP is detected using the standard Full-Speed SE0 condition.
- A configuration option shall allow a single SE0 bit to be treated as an end-of-packet indication.

The module shall support an oscillator test mode. When this mode is enabled, the module shall continuously drive a J/K alternating pattern on the transmit interface. In this mode, normal packet reception and host-SOF-based synchronization are not expected to occur.

The module shall only enable the USB pull-up when both the interface enable is set and VBUS presence is sensed. If either condition is not true, the pull-up shall be disabled.

## 4. USB Link State and Reset

The module shall monitor VBUS presence, the USB bus state, and start-of-frame reception to determine the current USB link state.

The module shall report the current link state using a link-state output. It shall also provide individual status indications for the following conditions:

- Disconnected
- Powered
- Reset
- Active
- Suspend
- Resume
- Host lost

The module shall behave as follows:

- **Disconnected:** The link is reported disconnected when VBUS is not sensed or when the interface pull-up is not enabled.
- **Powered:** When VBUS is sensed and the pull-up is enabled, the link is reported as powered until a USB reset is detected.
- **Reset:** A USB reset shall be detected when the bus is in the SE0 state for approximately 3 µs. When reset is detected, the module shall assert the reset status and cancel any in-progress transaction.
- **Active:** After reset, the link shall be reported active. This includes the period before the first host SOF is received and the normal active state thereafter.
- **Suspend:** The link shall be reported suspended when the bus remains in the idle J state for more than 3 ms.
- **Resume:** The module shall report resume when the bus leaves the suspend state, or when an explicit resume request is received while in the powered state. Resume ends when the link returns to the active state.
- **Host lost:** When the link is active but the expected host SOF packets are not received for four consecutive 1.005 ms frame-detection windows, the module shall assert the host-lost status. The condition clears when valid host SOF reception resumes.

When the interface is disabled or a USB reset is detected, the module shall assert the clear-address output so that the device address is forced to zero. This ensures the device responds only to the default address after reset or re-enable.

## 5. Start-of-Frame and Frame Number

The module shall maintain an 11-bit frame counter.

When the host sends a valid SOF packet, the module shall:

- Extract the frame number from the SOF packet.
- Load that frame number into the frame counter.
- Assert a host-SOF indication.

The host-SOF indication shall be asserted only for SOF packets actually received from the host. It shall not be asserted for locally generated frame events.

When the link is active but host SOFs are missing, the module shall continue to generate local frame boundaries at approximately 1 ms intervals. During each locally generated frame boundary, the module shall:

- Increment the frame counter.
- Assert a frame-start pulse.

The module shall assert a frame-start pulse whenever the frame counter changes, whether the change comes from a received host SOF or from a locally generated frame event.

The current frame number shall be available as a status output.

## 6. OUT and SETUP Transaction Reception

The module shall support reception of OUT and SETUP packets to enabled endpoints.

For each OUT or SETUP transaction, the module shall determine the response based on the endpoint state:

- If the endpoint is stalled, the module shall respond with STALL.
- If the endpoint is disabled for the transaction type, the module shall respond with NAK.
- If the endpoint is enabled but the packet cannot be accepted because no buffer is available or the receive FIFO cannot accept the result, the module shall respond with NAK.
- If the packet is accepted, the module shall receive the packet data and respond with ACK on successful completion.

An OUT or SETUP packet shall be accepted only when the following conditions are satisfied:

1. The endpoint is enabled for that direction and transaction type.
2. The endpoint is not stalled.
3. An available buffer ID is present in the available-buffer FIFO.
4. The receive FIFO has space for the resulting packet information entry.

When no available buffer ID is present, the module shall assert an event indicating that the available-buffer FIFO is empty. When the receive FIFO is full, the module shall assert an event indicating that the receive FIFO is full.

When a packet is accepted:

- The module shall use the buffer ID from the available-buffer FIFO as the destination buffer in the packet SRAM.
- The packet data bytes shall be written into that buffer in order.
- The packet CRC bytes may also be written into the buffer if they fit within the maximum packet size. CRC bytes are not included in the reported packet length.
- If the packet length is not a multiple of four bytes, the module shall still write the final partial word so that all received data bytes are visible in the packet buffer.
- On successful completion, the module shall write an entry to the receive FIFO. This entry shall contain:
  - The endpoint number.
  - An indication of whether the packet was an OUT or SETUP packet.
  - The received data length in bytes.
  - The buffer ID used for the packet.
- The buffer ID shall be consumed from the available-buffer FIFO exactly once for each successfully completed accepted packet.

The module shall support zero-length OUT and SETUP packets. A zero-length packet shall produce a receive-FIFO entry with a data length of zero.

If a received packet is aborted because of a CRC error, protocol error, or transaction rollback, the module shall:

- Not write an entry to the receive FIFO.
- Not consume the buffer ID for packet delivery.
- Not acknowledge the packet.
- Assert an OUT error indication.

The module shall generate a SETUP-received indication when a SETUP packet has been accepted and its receive-FIFO entry is written. The indication shall not be generated for a SETUP packet that was NAKed or stalled.

The module shall provide the endpoint number associated with the current OUT/SETUP transaction, together with a validity indication. If the endpoint number is outside the configured endpoint count, the validity indication shall be deasserted and the endpoint number shall be reported as zero.

## 7. IN Transaction Transmission

The module shall support transmission of data in response to IN transactions.

For each IN transaction to an enabled endpoint, the module shall determine the response as follows:

- If the endpoint is stalled, the module shall respond with STALL.
- If no transmit data is ready for the endpoint, the module shall respond with NAK.
- If transmit data is ready, the module shall transmit the queued packet from the packet SRAM.

A queued packet is described by:

- The buffer ID containing the packet data.
- The packet length in bytes.

The module shall read the packet data from the selected packet buffer and present it for transmission in the correct order. The module shall read additional words from the SRAM as needed until the full declared packet length has been transmitted.

The module shall support zero-length IN packets. A zero-length packet shall be transmitted when the declared length is zero.

When the host acknowledges the transmitted IN packet, the module shall assert a packet-sent indication for the endpoint.

If the IN transaction is aborted or rolled back, the module shall:

- Not assert the packet-sent indication.
- Assert an IN error indication.
- Leave the packet available for retry if the protocol requires it.

The module shall provide the endpoint number associated with the current IN transaction, together with a validity indication. If the endpoint number is outside the configured endpoint count, the validity indication shall be deasserted and the endpoint number shall be reported as zero.

The module shall support per-endpoint data-toggle clearing. When the clear-toggle control is asserted for an endpoint, the next data packet for that endpoint shall use the DATA0 toggle.

For isochronous endpoints, the module shall transfer packet data without normal ACK/NAK/STALL handshaking and without retry. The data-toggle sequencing shall not be applied to isochronous transfers.

## 8. SRAM Packet Buffer Interface

The module shall act as the USB-side master of the packet SRAM. It shall generate memory read requests for IN transmission and memory write requests for OUT/SETUP reception.

The module shall address the SRAM using:

- A buffer ID to select one of the available buffers.
- A word offset within that buffer to select a 32-bit word.

All writes performed during reception shall remain within the buffer selected by the available-buffer FIFO. The module shall not write beyond the configured maximum packet size boundary.

For receive writes:

- The module shall assemble incoming bytes into 32-bit words.
- Bytes shall be placed in the byte lane corresponding to their offset within the word.
- A full word shall be written when it has been completely assembled.
- A partial word shall be written when the packet completes, provided that partial word lies within the buffer.

For transmit reads:

- The module shall read the 32-bit word containing the next required byte.
- Data shall be extracted from the correct byte lane and supplied for transmission.

The module shall not generate memory accesses when no USB transaction requires them.

## 9. Status and Error Reporting

The module shall provide status outputs for the following protocol and bus error conditions:

- Received CRC error.
- Received PID error.
- Received bit-stuff error.
- IN transaction error or rollback.
- OUT transaction error or rollback.
- Host SOF loss.

These status outputs shall be asserted when the corresponding condition is detected. They are intended for interrupt generation and software diagnostics.

The module shall also provide event outputs for the following conditions:

- An OUT/SETUP packet arrives while the available-buffer FIFO is empty.
- An OUT/SETUP packet arrives while the receive FIFO is full.

These events allow software to react to interface backpressure.

## 10. Reset and Initialization

When the module is reset:

- The USB transmit output-enable shall be inactive.
- The USB pull-up shall be disabled.
- The link shall be reported as disconnected.
- The frame counter shall be cleared to zero.
- No FIFO entries shall be generated.
- No SRAM accesses shall be initiated.

When the module is disabled by software, the module shall:

- Disable the USB pull-up.
- Report the link as disconnected.
- Clear the device address.
- Stop accepting or transmitting USB packets.

When the module is enabled and VBUS is sensed, the module shall begin link-state detection and normal USB operation.

All outputs not covered above shall be deasserted or set to their inactive state while the module is reset or disabled.
